claims.text: Identical thermomechanical processing yields single-phase FCC microstructures in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and the quaternary and ternary alloys being compared.
Mn lowers the stacking-fault energy of the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy.
Mn produces composition-dependent magnetic interactions and magnetic frustration in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
The Mn-related reduction in stacking-fault energy and magnetic frustration promotes a deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation in the quinary alloy.
High-strain deformation of equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni produces a subtle but measurable HCP phase within its FCC matrix.
Deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation can proceed through stacking-fault structures promoted by chemical variation.
The deformation-induced transformation increases strain hardening.
The deformation-induced transformation delays necking or failure.
Equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets lacking Mn, or having a different Mn concentration, undergo less FCC-to-HCP transformation than the quinary alloy.
The quinary alloy will develop more nanoscale HCP material at high strain than the quaternary and ternary FCC baselines.
The quinary alloy will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate than the quaternary and ternary FCC baselines.
Transformation in the quinary alloy will improve load partitioning relative to the lower-order alloys.
The quaternary and ternary FCC baseline alloys are expected to show minimal or no deformation-induced transformation.
The extent of HCP formation is sensitive to temperature and strain rate.
The proposed comparison requires initially single-phase FCC alloys, otherwise identical processing and testing, and strains high enough to activate the proposed transformation.
The transformation mechanism is falsified if the quinary develops no statistically significant HCP phase, or an HCP fraction no greater than the lower-order controls, under the tested conditions.
